dedupe_keys.name: railway resilience to alpine hazards in austria obb infra protection works and infra wetter warning system

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes how ÖBB-Infrastruktur AG, the Austrian railway infrastructure manager, reduces risk from floods, debris flows, rockfalls, avalanches and landslides on a network that often runs along floodplains and steep slopes in the Eastern Alps. It combines structural protection such as avalanche galleries and rockfall nets, co-funded with regions and communities under the Hydraulic Engineering Assistance Act, with the infra:wetter weather monitoring and early warning system run with the private weather service UBIMET since 2005. infra:wetter merges ÖBB and GeoSphere Austria (ZAMG) stations, including 55 high-altitude stations, radar, satellite and forecasts with network data to send route-specific warnings to about 1,800 users and to flag critical meteorological conditions that trigger speed limits, closures or winter measures. The page cites the September 2024 floods in Lower Austria, with about EUR 100 million of direct damage on the western line, and costs from earlier events. It was first published in 2017, updated in 2026, and is accessible online as free HTML with references to the ENHANCE project and ÖBB reports. Caveats: infra:wetter is an internal ÖBB portal, not public data, and protection costs are not given as totals. The case illustrates emergency response, operations control and climate adaptation of a mountain rail network; related records are ERA RINF and the US railroad climate hazard exposure data.
name: Railway resilience to Alpine hazards in Austria (ÖBB Infra protection works and infra:wetter warning system)
outcomes: infra:wetter has issued route-specific warnings to about 1,800 users since 2005 and triggers pre-planned operational measures under critical meteorological conditions; the September 2024 floods still caused about EUR 100 million of direct damage.
provider: Climate-ADAPT (European Environment Agency), case study with ÖBB-Infrastruktur AG
resources_used: ÖBB and GeoSphere Austria weather stations
